papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
papers.abstract: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).

papers.title: Detecting Random Geometric Graphs with General Kernel
papers.abstract: We study testing a random geometric graph with a fixed kernel against an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph with the same edge density. Under the null hypothesis, the graph has $n$ vertices and independent edges with probability $p$. Under the alternative hypothesis, latent points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent and uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and edges are conditionally independent with probabilities $K(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)$, where $p=\mathbb{E}[K(\langle X_1,X_2\rangle)]$. The goal is to determine a critical dimension $d_\star = d_\star(n,K)$: the total variation distance between the two graph laws tends to one for $d\ll d_\star$ and to zero for $d\gg d_\star$. For dense graphs, [BDER16] established $d_\star\asymp n^3$ for hard threshold kernels, whereas [MWX26] proved $d_\star\asymp n^{3/4}$ for smooth kernels with $K'(0)\ne0$. We connect these results by characterizing the detection thresholds for kernels that need not be differentiable at zero. We also determine the thresholds for smooth kernels whose first nonzero derivative at zero has finite order greater than one. Throughout these classes, signed triangle or quadrilateral counts attain the optimal detection threshold. For certain nondifferentiable kernels, quadrilateral counts are optimal while triangle counts are suboptimal.

papers.title: Robust LassoNet: Enhancing Feature Selection in Neural Networks via Robust Loss Functions
papers.abstract: Feature selection in neural networks remains a challenging problem, particularly in the presence of noisy or contaminated data. LassoNet is a recent approach that addresses this issue by combining neural networks with hierarchical sparsity constraints, enabling simultaneous prediction and variable selection. However, its standard formulation relies on the mean squared error (MSE) loss, which is known to be highly sensitive to outliers. In this paper, we present Robust LassoNet, an extension of LassoNet that incorporates robust loss functions, such as Huber, Cauchy, Tukey's bisquare, and Nonnegative Garrote, to mitigate the effect of extreme observations. The proposed approach preserves the original optimization framework while improving stability under data contamination. Through experiments on synthetic and real datasets, we show that robust LassoNet significantly improves both predictive performance and feature selection accuracy in the presence of outliers or heavy tailed noise, while maintaining comparable performance in clean settings. These results highlight the importance of robustness in neural network based feature selection and suggest practical guidelines for choosing appropriate loss functions.

papers.title: Tandem Queues with Hybrid Abandonment in Heavy Traffic
papers.abstract: Hybrid-abandonment systems, where jobs abandon from certain stages of service but not others, occur frequently in medical, service, and computing systems. Abandonment affects the heavy-traffic behavior of both the stages with and without abandonment. In contrast to existing heavy-traffic works that focus on cases where there is abandonment at either all stages or no stages, we focus on the heavy-traffic behavior for these hybrid-abandonment systems. We provide the first heavy-traffic characterization of the second queue length in a two-stage tandem queue with abandonment only in the first stage. We characterize the scaled mean of the second stage queue length and prove that the scaled second queue length is asymptotically exponentially distributed and asymptotically independent of the first stage queue length. We derive our results by analyzing Markovian arrival process queues with countably infinite phases. We do this by extending techniques used to analyze queues with Markov-modulated arrivals to the broader class of infinite Markovian arrival process queues. We prove asymptotic results for a more general infinite phase process condition, an infinite birth-death phase process, and the hybrid-abandonment tandem case. We also empirically demonstrate that our heavy-traffic approximations are good approximations across various system settings.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations
papers.abstract: Autonomous small-body proximity operations require continuous-thrust guidance under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure (SRP), and stochastic disturbances. We combine iterative covariance steering (iCS) with $L_1$ distributionally robust adaptive control ($L_1$-DRAC) to provide risk-aware collision avoidance despite mismatch between the nominal planning model and the true dynamics. Iterative covariance steering plans a nominal feedback policy satisfying distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints, while $L_1$-DRAC compensates for dynamics uncertainty and bounds the residual distributional mismatch through a Wasserstein radius used by the planner. In $\mathbf{1000}$ paired Monte Carlo trials with gravity, SRP, and diffusion mismatch, $L_1$-DRAC adaptive control reduces the keep-out violation rate from $\mathbf{32.7\%}$ to $\mathbf{0.2\%}$ and the physical collision rate from $\mathbf{16.4\%}$ to zero, without actuator saturation.

papers.title: Weighted derivative estimates for Kolmogorov equations
papers.abstract: For diffusions whose coefficients are smooth, with at most linear growth and bounded derivatives of higher order, we establish explicit pointwise bounds on the spatial derivatives of the classical solution to the Cauchy problem with polynomially growing initial data. We also obtain explicit growth estimates for the derivatives of the SDE with respect to the initial data. The proofs combine Lyapunov functions and Markov semigroups on weighted spaces with Kunita's theory of the differentiable dependence of SDE solutions on the initial data.

papers.title: An efficient stochastic generalized method of moments estimator for nonlinear moment models
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic properties of the nonlinear stochastic GMM algorithm proposed by Chen, Lee, Liao, Seo, Shin and Song for recursively estimating parameters defined by possibly nonlinear and overidentified moment restrictions $\E[g(X,\beta^*)]=0$. Each observation updates estimates of the moment Jacobian, inverse covariance matrix and Gauss--Newton preconditioner at a cost independent of sample size. For linear and nonlinear instrumental-variable moments, we derive an exact rank-two Sherman--Morrison--Woodbury update. The algorithm combines preconditioned stochastic approximation with iterate averaging. Under a preconditioned monotonicity condition, satisfied globally in linear models and locally around a consistent pilot estimate in general, we establish almost sure convergence and rates, as well as a functional central limit theorem with the efficient GMM variance. These results require four moments of the moment function and its Jacobian when the step exponent exceeds $2/3$. The inverse Gauss--Newton matrix consistently estimates this variance, and a projected linearised statistic enables online testing of overidentifying restrictions. We extend the results to $L$-dependent data with long-run variance weights under stronger moment assumptions. Simulations show that the averaged estimator approaches offline two-step GMM in accuracy and coverage at $10^6$ observations, while requiring a fraction of its computing time and fixed memory at up to $10^7$ observations. The online test achieves correct size and comparable power. In an application estimating the effect of a third child on weeks worked using $254{,}654$ women from the 1980 US Census, single-pass estimates agree with offline GMM within a fraction of a standard error on average across data orderings, and both methods yield the same overidentification-test conclusion in most orderings.

papers.title: Existence of ergodic invariant measures for 3D Navier-Stokes eqs with superlinear noise
papers.abstract: We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain $D\subset \mathbb R^3$. It has been proved in arXiv:2609.08284 that these equations have a unique solution - globally defined in time - when a superlinear noise is introduced and the initial velocity belongs to the space $V$ of divergence-free $H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^3)$-vector fields. Here we show that the same result holds when there is also an additive noise and a deterministic forcing term. Moreover, when the deterministic forcing term is time-independent we prove the existence of at least one invariant measure for this stochastic equation. This is obtained by the Krylov-Bogoliubov method, based on tightness and Feller property in $V$. Finally, we show that the set of invariant measures contains one ergodic invariant measure.

papers.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
papers.abstract: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.

papers.title: Statistical inference for rough Burgers-type stochastic partial differential equations
authors: Simon Chony Acosta Christian Olivera Ciprian Tudor
papers.abstract: We consider the Burgers-type stochastic PDE \[ du = \theta\,\partial_x^2 u\,dt + f(u)\,dt + g(u)\,\partial_x u\,dt + \sigma\,dW(t), \] driven by space--time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, where \(\theta>0\) is the diffusivity parameter and \(\sigma>0\) the noise intensity. The transport term \(g(u)\,\partial_x u\) admits no classical interpretation, and we work with the mild solutions defined via rough paths following~\cite{Hairer2011}, for which the solution decomposes as \(u=\psi+R\) with \(\psi\) a stationary centred Gaussian process solving a damped stochastic heat equation and \(R\) a remainder. We first show that, away from the initial time, \(R\) is Lipschitz in space and H\"older in time of order strictly greater than \(1/2\), hence strictly smoother than \(\psi\) in both variables. We then compute exactly the spatial quadratic variation and the temporal quartic variation of \(\psi\), almost surely and not merely in \(L^{2}(\Omega)\), and prove that the corresponding variations of \(u\) are unaffected by the remainder. Combined with an exact time-scaling identity, this separation of regularity scales yields strongly consistent pathwise estimators of \(\theta\). To our knowledge this is the first inference procedure for an SPDE whose solution is defined only pathwise, as a measurable function of a rough path, rather than as an It\^o process.

papers.title: Why does entropy drive evolution equations?
papers.abstract: `Entropy' appears as driving force in many different evolution equations, both deterministic and stochastic, and in these equations this `entropy' also takes different forms. We show how all these examples can be understood as different instances of a common principle: Entropy drives evolutions because it characterizes the invariant measure of an underlying stochastic process. This interpretation explains the appearance of entropy, the different forms that entropy takes in these equations, and how entropy `drives' these evolution equations. We illustrate this common structure with examples from stochastic processes, gradient flows, and GENERIC systems.

papers.title: $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)_2$ Theory from many-body quantum Gibbs states
papers.abstract: We derive the $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)_2$ measure on the two-dimensional unit torus as the rigorous limit of many-body quantum Gibbs states. In particular, the quantum model corresponding to the $\Phi^{2p}_2$ measure is formulated in the grand-canonical ensemble with a general symmetric $p$-body interaction potential which is not required to have a factorized form. Unlike in the $\Phi^4_2$ case investigated by Fr\"ohlich--Knowles--Schlein--Sohinger in \cite{FKSS25}, in the treatment of higher-order interactions, Wick renormalization generates a full hierarchy of lower-order interactions which we organize systematically using a graphical formalism. One key ingredient of our analysis is a logarithmic stability estimate for both the nonlocal Hartree functional and the many-body Hamiltonian that is uniform in the interaction range, allowing us to use the positivity of the leading $p$-body interaction to control all lower-order terms generated by the Wick counterterms.

papers.title: Dynamical classical-field limit of Bosonic Gibbs states: Renormalized Hartree NLS correlations in 2D and 3D
papers.abstract: In this paper we derive the time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation on the torus $\mathbb T^d$, $d=2,3$, from the corresponding bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics. In contrast with the 1D problem studied earlier by Fr\"ohlich, Knowles, Schlein and Sohinger, in higher dimensions the scaled quantum particle number is not uniformly bounded and the relevant classical fields require Wick renormalization. Our proof combines convergence of the quantum generators in weighted Hilbert spaces with uniqueness for positive solutions of the limiting Liouville equation that are dominated by the Gibbs measure.

papers.title: On the composition of permutons
papers.abstract: Permutons can be thought of as "continuum limits" of permutations of diverging size, which encode information about the number of occurrences of any given finite subpattern. We construct a natural composition operation on permutons, analogous to composition of permutations, and explore its properties via a correspondence between permutons, Markov kernels, and Markov operators. We show that no extension of permutation composition to permutons can be (jointly) continuous with respect to the usual "weak" topology on permutons, but we construct a "strong" topology with respect to which composition is jointly continuous. Moreover, we characterize strong convergence of sequences of permutations of diverging size: a sequence of permutations converges strongly if and only if it converges weakly and its limit is the transpose of the graph of a measure-preserving function. The key insight behind these results is to apply functional analysis to certain operators associated to permutons; with this shift in perspective, our results have elegant and relatively "soft" proofs. As an application, we describe the permuton limit of a product of finitely many independent uniformly sampled separable permutations and give a formula for the expectation of this limit. We also show that in this case, as the number of compositions goes to infinity, the aforementioned expectation tends to the uniform permuton.

papers.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
papers.abstract: We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,\lambda \in (0,1)$: \[ \gamma_{\Sigma_1}(K)^{1-p} \gamma_{\Sigma_2}(L)^p \le \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-\lambda} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}{\lambda} \right)^p \right)^{n} \gamma_{\Gamma}((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L) , \] whenever $\Gamma \leq \Sigma_1 \sharp_p \Sigma_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $\Sigma_1 = \Sigma_2 = \Gamma$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=\lambda$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$: \[ \gamma(a K)^{1-\lambda} \gamma(b L)^{\lambda} \leq \gamma \left ( a^{1-\lambda} b^\lambda \left ((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.

papers.title: Quantum-assisted rendezvous on hypercubes: a quantum Bernoulli noise approach
papers.abstract: We study quantum-assisted balanced rendezvous on the $d$-dimensional hypercube in a one-step two-agent quantum-walk framework, where the two agents move the same Hamming distance and meet at a common midpoint. The key structure is a projective $t$-sphere resolution, which governs exact finite-dimensional quantum attainment. Its scalar analogue recovers the corresponding classical characterization. We characterize finite-dimensional quantum attainment of the no-signalling benchmark, construct quantum strategies from projective sphere resolutions, and establish a rigidity theorem for optimal finite-dimensional strategies. A marked difference appears between nearest-neighbor and higher-cardinality updates: quantum advantage can occur in the former, whereas in the latter the geometry of the relevant Hamming spheres rules out exact finite-dimensional attainment of the no-signalling value. Together, these results connect quantum-walk dynamics, Hamming-sphere geometry, and quantum rendezvous within the quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN) framework.

papers.title: Markovian Random Words, a Gaussian Random Matrix Model and Beyond
papers.abstract: After centering and scaling, the length of the longest weakly increasing subsequence of a finite-state Markov random word converges to a Brownian last-passage functional with dependent components. We investigate when this functional, and more generally the limiting RSK Young-diagram shape, admits a Gaussian random-matrix representation. We introduce Hermitian Gaussian matrices with correlated diagonal entries and show that isotropy of the Brownian covariance on the trace-zero hyperplane yields such a representation. Within this natural class of Hermitian models with independent Gaussian off-diagonal entries, we prove a rigidity theorem showing that isotropy, together with equality of the off-diagonal variances, characterizes the conditional largest-eigenvalue representation. Explicit three-letter non-cyclic Markov chains demonstrate that this representation is not universal: the limiting Brownian functional may fail to have the law of the largest eigenvalue of any centered jointly Gaussian $3\times 3$ Hermitian matrix. Finally, we extend the random-matrix identification to chains with non-uniform stationary distributions and to countable state spaces.

papers.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous--Broder Theorem
papers.abstract: Random spanning forests provide probability models for partitions and Monte Carlo methods on graphs. In these applications, the distribution produced by a sampler determines which forest functionals can be estimated. The Aldous--Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but a direct calculation requires summing over all orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered. We evaluate this sum through an identity for rooted forests and real matrices with zero row sums. Under a nonsingularity condition on the principal submatrices encountered during growth, the sum of products of harmonic extension entries equals a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots. With one root, the sum is one. The identity gives a direct proof of the extended Aldous--Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state, without assuming reversibility or bidirectional transition support. It also gives the conditional distribution of the discovery order and the law of the forest obtained by stopping after all nonroot vertices have been visited. A completion weight describes the difference between this stopped-walk law and the weight-proportional forest law, including the support restriction needed for importance correction. Numerical examples illustrate the sampling implications. The identity, the Aldous--Broder theorem, and the stopped-forest law are formalized in Lean4.

papers.title: Dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for $\mathbb R^2$-valued polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for polynomial mappings $(f_1,f_2)\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^2$ of degree at most $d$. For product probability measures whose one-dimensional marginals have densities bounded by $1$, we obtain a lower bound for the integral of the Gram determinant of $\nabla f_1$ and $\nabla f_2$ in terms of the Gram determinant of the $d$-th derivative tensors $D^df_1$ and $D^df_2$, with a constant depending only on $d$. For pairs in a fixed Wiener chaos, the resulting Gaussian inequality answers a question of Nourdin, Nualart, and Poly concerning a lower bound for the expectation of the Malliavin determinant in terms of the determinant of the covariance matrix.

papers.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
papers.abstract: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.

papers.title: Exact bounds on the distribution function of isotropic log-concave distributions
papers.abstract: For each real $b$, exact upper and lower bounds on the probability $\mathsf P(X\ge b)$ over all random variables $X$ with log-concave p.d.f.'s such that $\mathsf E X=0$ and $\mathsf E X^2=1$ are obtained, as well as the best constant factor $C$ in the inequality $\mathsf P(X\ge b)\le C e^{-b}$ for all real $b\ge0$. Exact upper and lower bounds on the corresponding exponential moments (Proposition 9.4) and explicit exponentially decreasing upper bounds on the mentioned p.d.f.'s (Propositions 9.2 and 9.3) are given as well. Some general results concerning log-concave p.d.f.'s are also obtained.

papers.title: Critical Ising model as the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory
papers.abstract: We construct a linear map from the space of spin polynomials in the critical Ising model on a lattice to the state space of the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory. The kernel of the map consists precisely of null fields, i.e., spin polynomials that vanish in all correlations. For a polynomial $\Op$ which is not a null field, we define its scaling dimension $\Delta_{\Op}\in\Z_{\geq0}\cup(\Z_{\geq0}+\frac{1}{8}),$ to be the lowest $\Loper{0}+\Loperbar{0}$ eigenvalue in the decomposition of its image into homogeneous components. We show that as the mesh size $\delta$ goes to zero, the rescaled field $\delta^{-\Delta_{\Op}}\Op$ has a non-trivial scaling limit, when inserted in correlations with other such fields. Moreover, all these limits can be expressed in terms of correlations of primary fields of $M(4,3)$ and the Virasoro action in the continuum. The highest weight vectors of $M(4,3)$, the joint eigenvectors of $\Loper{0}$ and $\Loperbar{0}$ with the same eigenvalues $0,1/16,1/2$ for both, are the images of the constant $1$, the spin at a single lattice vertex, and the energy at a single lattice edge, respectively. For the proof, we construct a map from a larger lattice field space, accommodating also fermion and disorder insertions, to a direct sum of two fermionic Fock spaces. This direct sum contains contains the state spaces of both the $M(4,3)$ and the free fermion CFT. The main technical ingredient of the proof is a new version of the exact fermionic current action on the space of lattice local fields due to C. Hongler, K.K. and F. Viklund, combined with some new advances in discrete complex analysis. Our results are valid on arbitrary isoradial graphs.

papers.title: BKT transition for $\mathsf{Sine}_\beta$
papers.abstract: We prove the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase transition in the large-distance behaviour of the two-point correlation function of the $\mathsf{Sine}_\beta$ point process for all $\beta>0$, confirming the first term of an asymptotic expansion predicted by Forrester.

papers.title: TAP variational formula for 2-spin models with general interaction matrix and marginality
papers.abstract: We establish a Thouless--Anderson--Palmer (TAP) variational formula for the free energy of spherical $2$-spin models whose interaction matrices have a compactly supported limiting spectral distribution. The formula holds at every inverse temperature and, in particular, extends the TAP representation previously obtained for the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main contribution is a new microcanonical proof designed to handle marginality. We partition the sphere according to the smallest collection of top eigendirections carrying a prescribed fraction of the norm. On every element of this partition, the remaining degrees of freedom are effectively at high temperature and their contribution can be computed through spherical-integral asymptotics. The resulting auxiliary variational problem separates the macroscopic low-temperature contribution from the high-temperature fluctuation term; its maximization recovers the usual TAP functional and Plefka condition. This decomposition also shows why neighborhoods of the TAP maximizers alone do not capture the Gibbs mass: all eigendirections associated with large eigenvalues contribute on the same exponential scale, a manifestation of the marginality of spherical $2$-spin states.

papers.title: Fine asymptotics of the magnetization of the annealed dilute Curie-Weiss model
papers.abstract: We consider the dilute Curie-Weiss model of size $N$, which is a generalization of the classical Curie-Weiss model in which the dependency structure between the spins is encoded not by the complete graph but by the (directed) Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph on $N$ vertices in which every edge appears independently with probability $p(N)$. In the high-temperature regime with an external magnetic field ($0<\beta<1,h\in\mathbb{R}$) we prove for $p^{3}N^{2}\to\infty$ sharp cumulant bounds for the magnetization under the annealed Gibbs measure, which imply a central limit theorem with rate, moderate and large deviation principles, a concentration inequality, a normal approximation with Cram\'er correction and mod-Gaussian convergence.

papers.title: Functional limit theorems for weighted occupation times of supercritical superprocesses
papers.abstract: Suppose $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a supercritical superprocess with a non-local branching mechanism on a Lusin space $E$, whose mean semigroup admits a positive leading eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ with a bounded positive eigenfunction $\varphi$ and a finite eigenmeasure $\widetilde{\varphi}$. Let $Y_t:=\int_0^t X_s\mathrm{d}s$ be its occupation measure. We first prove a law of large numbers, that is, for every bounded measurable function $f$, $e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ converges in $L^2$ to $\lambda_1^{-1}\langle f,\widetilde{\varphi}\rangle W^\varphi_\infty$, where $W^\varphi_\infty$ is the limit of the martingale $W^\varphi_t:=e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle\varphi,X_t\rangle$. We then establish functional central limit theorems for the fluctuations of $\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ around this random centering. We show that the normalisation and the limit are determined by the spectral decay rate of $f$ compared with the critical value $\lambda_1/2$, and there are three possible regimes: after suitable normalisation, the fluctuation process converges in distribution in $\mathcal{C}[0,+\infty)$ either to a mixed Gaussian process $\sqrt{W^{\varphi}_{\infty}}G(f)$, or to a constant Gaussian process with random variance depending on $W^{\varphi}_{\infty}$, or to a non-Gaussian limit given by the limit of a martingale associated with the spectral projection of $f$. These results are the occupation-time counterparts of the fluctuation theorems for linear functionals of supercritical non-local branching superprocesses.

papers.title: Ancestral circulation beyond two Fleming-Viot particles
papers.abstract: Reversible motion can produce a directed circulation of surviving ancestry in a \FV\ particle system. We prove that two particles are the exact threshold for universal ancestral balance in finite systems with uniform copying. For two particles, the stationary current of surviving labels vanishes for every finite irreducible reversible Markov chain and every positive killing vector. On a fixed complete three-state graph, nonzero circulation occurs for each population size at least three on an open dense set of killing vectors of full Lebesgue measure. A single killing vector produces circulation simultaneously for every population size at least three, and such vectors form a dense $G_\delta$ set of full measure. The current is divergence free and vanishes on bridges, so three sites and three particles are the smallest possible setting for circulation. We also identify the probabilistic effect of this circulation: for sufficiently rare transplants, migration followed by fixation is more likely in one direction than in the reverse direction.

papers.title: Stochastic Modelling of Telomere Length Dynamics During Hematopoiesis
papers.abstract: We introduce a new stochastic model of telomere length dynamics during hematopoiesis. The numerous cell divisions occurring in this setting makes telomere length dynamics, and in particular their attrition, a crucial aspect of hematopoiesis. After recalling the main aspect of the biological setting, we describe an individual based model of hematopoietic population cells. We then study its behaviour in the large population limit, as well as its fluctuations.

papers.title: Effective-dimension bounds in the central limit theorem for centered Euclidean balls
papers.abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic Gaussian approximation bound over centered Euclidean balls for sums of independent, not necessarily identically distributed, random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\). Let \(S_n\) denote the sum, let \(\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\), and let \(G\sim N(0,\Sigma)\). Define the effective rank and the normalized squared spectral mass by \[ r(\Sigma)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma}{\|\Sigma\|}, \qquad v(\Sigma)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2)}{\|\Sigma\|^2}. \] Under a uniform directional fourth-moment condition, covariance-balance assumptions, and the spectral conditions \(r(\Sigma)\le C_\Sigma v(\Sigma)\) and \(v(\Sigma)\ge6\), we prove \[ \sup_{z\ge0} \left| \mathbb P\{\|S_n\|^2\le z\} - \mathbb P\{\|G\|^2\le z\} \right| \le C\,\frac{r(\Sigma)^{3/2}}{n}. \] The constant depends only on the fixed parameters in the assumptions and is independent of the ambient dimension and individual small eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. The bound is uniform at the endpoint \(v(\Sigma)=6\), without a logarithmic loss. Its main feature is the combination of the \(n^{-1}\) rate with dependence on effective rank, including this endpoint. Consequently, the bound can vanish when \(r(\Sigma)=o(n^{2/3})\), even when \(p\) is much larger than \(n\). The same estimate extends to random elements of a separable Hilbert space with trace class covariance. The proof builds on the Fourier and symmetrization methods of \citet{GoetzeZaitsev2014}, combined with moment matching, truncation, and comparison estimates that retain the covariance structure.

papers.title: Large deviations for additive functionals of one-dimensional zero-range processes
papers.abstract: We prove a large deviation principle for additive functionals of local Lipschitz functions of a one-dimensional symmetric zero-range process on the diffusive scale. The rate function is obtained from the dynamical large deviation principle for the empirical density and is characterized by a variational constraint involving the density at a fixed spatial point. On the microscopic side, a super-exponential replacement is needed to replace the local observable with a function of the empirical density. On the macroscopic side, the spatial regularity enjoyed by finite-rate trajectories is needed to pass from spatial averages to point evaluation.
